facts.F221: Composition-root rule, one oracle file per slice (nwdes approval freezes each slice bytes, so no slice edits an earlier one): S1 CompositionRootNamesModulesOnlyThroughTheirModuleArchUnitTest lists FlowMetrics, Forecasting, Promises, Licensing, Access; S2 CompositionRootNamesTheOtherModulesOnlyThroughTheirModuleArchUnitTest lists WorkItems, TrackerIntegration, Refinement, Reports, OrganisationSetup; together they are the ten-context rule. Each asserts, per listed context: its <X>Module exists in Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.<X> with Add<X>; only Program names it; Program registers no type of that context, where registers means the type is a generic argument of a call to an IServiceCollection registration extension (Add*, TryAdd*, Configure*, AddHostedService) or of GetService/GetRequiredService, read from the IL of Program and its compiler-made nested types; allowed, by full name and compared both ways, in four declared categories: (1) the handler block entries of that context; (2) the order-kept registrations of that context; (3) the host set-up lookups Program makes with GetRequiredService (Forecasting ForecastLane in PrintSystemInfo, Access IOidcGroupSnapshotWriter in the OIDC token-validated event), compared apart from registrations; (4) cross-context wiring kept in Program: the context types named by a registration statement that names types of two contexts. Measured at 1c51ec97e, the only such statements outside the handler block are Program.cs:1475 AddScoped<IDescriptionBlockMerger, DeliveryForecastBlockRenderer> (TrackerIntegration + Promises), :1481 AddScoped<IThroughputFilter>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<ForecastFilterRuleService>()), :1483 IForecastDataSufficiency and :1484 IHowManyForecaster, both from ForecastingAnswersToFlowMetrics (FlowMetrics + Forecasting). S1 category 4 entries: FlowMetrics registered IThroughputFilter, IForecastDataSufficiency, IHowManyForecaster (FlowMetrics.Application); Forecasting looked up ForecastFilterRuleService, ForecastingAnswersToFlowMetrics (Forecasting.Application); Promises registered DeliveryForecastBlockRenderer (Promises.Application). S2 category 4 entry: TrackerIntegration registered IDescriptionBlockMerger (TrackerIntegration.Application). Method for S2 and any later context: before writing its list, list every registration statement of Program (statements joined across lines, handler block excluded) whose type names resolve to declarations under two different Modules/<X> folders, Contracts included; then confirm by a trial move whose Architecture run names no <X>Module in R-C1 or in another context's boundary rule. The call reading is a new support CompositionRootRegistrations written with the S1 oracle and only read afterwards. facts.F223: Own-context root (maintainer decision 2026-11-26): a context's own <X>Module (Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.<X>.<X>Module) counts as the composition root, but only for the rules about its own context: adapters reached only by the composition root, only the composition root creates the forecast threads, and the membership lists, which gain the <X>Module entry. It is never a composition root for another context: a registration statement that names types of two contexts (one context's type built from, or registered as, another context's service) stays in Program as cross-context wiring, so no new cross-context edge appears and feature A's 73-edge R-C1 list and its surface rows stay unchanged. Rule edits are the narrowest that express this: an exact <X>Module full name or file path, never a namespace-wide exemption, and no rule or list is loosened across contexts; each edit is proven by a reverted probe recorded as a craft command. The preservation pin StartUpRegistrationsPreservationTest.cs names types by today's full names on purpose and is exempt, by its exact file name, from the old-name sweep of ContextContractsMembershipArchUnitTest; the exemption lands in the pin's own first commit and leaves with the pin at S3. Feature A's oracle files and the boundary and membership tests these edits touch are declared targets of the slice whose move makes them fail; ModuleRules.cs and ContextContractsArchUnitTest.cs need no edit, because every production call site passes the root and the set-aside namespaces as arguments and the cross-context lines stay in Program. Pattern used for both-ways adapter rules: composition root = the exact <X>Module full name, set-aside namespaces = the context's namespaces below its root (^Lighthouse\.Backend\.Modules\.<X>\.), so <X>Module is the one outside reacher and Program reaching the adapters fails.
